_meta.indication: NEXOBRID is indicated for eschar removal in adults with deep partial thickness (DPT) and/or full thickness (FT) thermal burns.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded, three-arm study comparing NEXOBRID, standard of care (SOC), and gel vehicle.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with deep partial thickness (DPT) and/or full thickness (FT) thermal burns of 3-30% BSA.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: incidence of >=95% eschar removal at the end of the topical treatment period (NEXOBRID vs. vehicle).
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 175 subjects were randomized 3:3:1 (NEXOBRID:SOC:gel vehicle); 169 treated. Primary endpoint analysis: NEXOBRID N=75, Gel Vehicle N=25.
pivotal_trials.result: >=95% eschar removal: 93% (70/75) NEXOBRID vs 4% (1/25) gel vehicle, treatment difference 89% (95% CI 74%, 96%). Incidence of surgical excision for eschar removal: 4% (3/75) NEXOBRID vs 72% (54/75) SOC, difference -68% (95% CI -78%, -56%).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized, two-arm study comparing NEXOBRID to SOC.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with DPT and/or FT thermal burns of 5-24% BSA; efficacy analyzed on DPT burns only.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Incidence of surgical (excision) eschar removal, NEXOBRID vs SOC.
pivotal_trials.n: Enrolled 182 subjects; 156 randomized. Efficacy (DPT wounds): NEXOBRID 106 wounds in 49 subjects, SOC 88 wounds in 48 subjects.
pivotal_trials.result: Incidence of excision for eschar removal (per wound): 15% (16/106 wounds) NEXOBRID vs 63% (55/88 wounds) SOC, difference -47% (95% CI -59%, -34%); per subject: 22% (11/49) vs 77% (37/48), difference -55% (95% CI -71%, -38%).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were pruritus and pyrexia. In the integrated safety analysis (NEXOBRID N=177 vs SOC N=149): pruritus 15% vs 13%, pyrexia 12% vs 9%, wound complication 9% vs 6.0%, anemia 6% vs 5%. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis have been reported with postmarketing use.
target_moa: The mixture of proteolytic enzymes in NEXOBRID dissolves burn wound eschar; the effect is mediated by proteolytic activity that selectively debrides the eschar or denatured collagen. The specific components responsible have not been identified.
modality: Enzyme (mixture of proteolytic enzymes extracted from the stems of pineapple plants, composed mainly of stem bromelain, ananain and other proteins; a botanical/biologic drug product for topical use).

rems.type: No REMS; REMS review was deferred and the label contains no REMS/Medication Guide.

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic; devices and companion diagnostic issues were not applicable.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened for this application.

basis.text: The Complete Response was issued due to numerous product quality (PQ) and Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) deficiencies, including significant unblinding/GCP issues in Study MW2010-03-02 (DETECT).

citations.quote: The application received a Complete Response on 06/25/2021 due to numerous product quality (PQ) and Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) deficiencies.

During the clinical site inspections for Study MW2010-03-02, a significant number of potential unblinding events were identified for assessments that were supposed to be conducted by blinded assessors.

During routine PDUFA and for-cause good clinical practice (GCP) inspections for Protocol MW2010-03-02, significant issues related to the conduct of the trial and GCP noncompliance were observed that impact the reliability of the eschar removal and wound closure assessments made by the first and second blinded assessors.
